EIGHT COLUMNS, NAMED FROM THE PRINTED HEADER, verbatim: FORWARD | COMMITTMENTS [sic] | ABATEMENTS | PAYMENTS | REFUNDS | TRANSFER | ADJUSTMENTS | BALANCES. 28 ROWS CLOSE INDEPENDENTLY TO THE CENT on forward + commitments + abatements + payments + refunds + transfer + adjustments = balances; the page prints its negatives in PARENTHESES per column, so the identity is a signed SUM and not a subtraction. Measured page rotation -0.01095, measured row pitch 0.01210, band half of that (rule 13b). THE REFUSAL REASON ON RECORD IS FALSE: `receivables-refused.csv` says of FY2019 pages 53, 54 and 55 `no BALANCES column printed, so no row can be proved`. BALANCES IS PRINTED -- it is the eighth column of the printed header and it is reproduced here; the whole header band sits inside the top 22.7% of the page that the COMMITTED clipped OCR render discarded, so the extractor could not see the column it then reported as absent (rule 13c, a statement about our instrument published as a statement about the town). ROW KEYS ARE QUALIFIED BY THEIR PRINTED SECTION because a label is not a key: this page prints `LEVY OF 2007` through `LEVY OF 2018` under TWO different section headings, and keying on the label alone would collapse 24 rows into 12 and let the file pass with reduced power. THE FIRST ROW OF THIS PAGE CARRIES NO SECTION HEADING and is keyed `LEVY OF 2019` unqualified. The page was cropped and looked at at 3x to settle it: it opens with a bare `LEVY OF 2019` line and the next printed heading, `MOTOR VEHICLE EXCISE`, comes BELOW it. It is almost certainly the PERSONAL PROPERTY block continuing from page 53, which ends at LEVY OF 2018 -- but page 54 does not restate the heading, so nesting it under PERSONAL PROPERTY would be our claim and not the document's.  WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the run's GRAND TOTAL is printed on page 55 and is the total of the WHOLE run (53-55); it is not footed here against the three pages' rows, and no page-level subtotal is printed to foot each page on its own.
